Required-key deny (lines 35-42), identity deny (lines 44-56), date deny (lines 58-71), futurity deny (lines 73-87): all gate on scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload → none fire. scp_r_002_test.rego has no test for [{"custom": "x"}] or [{}]. R1 finding F-COR-008 (MIN) identified this gap; SAFETY-001 fix addressed only the scalar/non-object entry case; the object-with-unknown-keys case was left unaddressed. With the scalar bypass now closed, this is the sole remaining structural bypass of SCP-R-002.
findings.impact: An adversary submitting [{}] or [{"foo":"bar"}] as waivers.json bypasses all five deny branches of SCP-R-002 with zero findings. The bypass is trivially constructable and is not caught by the schema validation except under scp_bypass=true. After SAFETY-001 fixed the scalar case, this object-bypass is the only remaining path to completely avoid SCP-R-002 enforcement, elevating its priority relative to its R1 MIN rating.
findings.mitigation: Replace the two-clause scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload helper with a single always-true clause for non-empty arrays: 'scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload if { is_array(input); count(input) > 0 }'. Keep the empty-array clause. This ensures the required-key/identity/date deny rules evaluate every object entry regardless of which keys it contains; the is_object guard in each deny rule handles non-object entries that the first deny rule already catches. Add test_scp_r_002_denies_empty_object_entry with input_value := [{}] expecting at minimum denies for approved_by, expires_at, created_at, reason, and rule_id/finding_id.

findings.claim: The Regal linter binary is downloaded and installed using only a post-download smoke test (regal version); unlike OPA (Sigstore attestation + SHA256) and Conftest (archive SHA256 + binary SHA256), Regal has no cryptographic supply-chain verification, breaking the integrity invariant the workflow establishes for its other tool dependencies.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:224-226 — 'curl ... ${REGAL_REPO}/${REGAL_ASSET} --output ${BIN_DIR}/regal; chmod +x; regal version'. No SHA256 field exists in scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for regal. REGAL_VERSION is hardcoded inline at line 144 rather than read from scripts/.tool-versions via read_tool_version. Compare: OPA at lines 207-211 uses resolve_opa (SHA256 via verify_sha256) then gh attestation verify. Conftest at lines 213-221 uses resolve_conftest (archive SHA256 + binary SHA256). The verify_sha256 helper at lines 171-177 is defined but never called for Regal. R1 SAFETY-005 (MIN) identified this; it was not in the fr1 closure set.
findings.impact: A compromised Regal release artifact (MITM or upstream compromise) would execute in the CI runner with full access to the checked-out repository. Because Regal runs before the OPA coverage gate and conftest steps, a malicious binary could exfiltrate repository secrets, tamper with output artifacts (policy-findings.json, disabled-rules.json), or suppress lint violations to allow non-conforming policies to merge. The risk is lower than for OPA/Conftest because Regal's output affects only lint step results, not the Rego evaluation that drives the threshold gate.
findings.mitigation: Add regal sha256 entries to scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for linux-x64 and linux-arm64. Move REGAL_VERSION from the inline hardcode (line 144) to scripts/.tool-versions and read it via read_tool_version. Apply verify_sha256 to the downloaded binary after chmod. When Regal publishes Sigstore attestations, add gh attestation verify on parity with OPA.

findings.claim: SCP-R-002 tests do not have a time-injection helper (analogous to SCP-R-001's scp_r_001_results_at(input, now_ns)), making the expires_at == now boundary condition untestable deterministically and creating an inconsistent test isolation pattern between the two time-sensitive rules.
findings.evidence: scp_r_001_test.rego:13-18 — defines scp_r_001_results_at(input_value, now_ns) using 'with main.scp_r_001_now_ns as now_ns', enabling precise boundary testing. SCP-R-001.rego:24 — scp_r_001_now_ns := time.now_ns() is a module-level constant overridable via 'with'. scp_r_002_test.rego — contains no scp_r_002_results_at helper. SCP-R-002.rego:16 — scp_r_002_now_ns := time.now_ns() is structurally identical to the R-001 pattern and is overridable in the same way. The expiry deny rule (lines 73-87) uses expiry_ns <= scp_r_002_now_ns; the boundary condition expiry_ns == scp_r_002_now_ns is currently covered only by the test using expires_at: '2020-01-01' (clearly in the past) and the allow tests using '2099-...' (clearly in the future). The exact-equality edge is not tested.
findings.impact: The boundary condition 'waiver expires exactly at evaluation time' cannot be unit-tested deterministically without the injection helper. Tests rely on date margins rather than precise time control, which makes future tests fragile if written with near-future dates. The inconsistency also means contributors adding tests for SCP-R-002 time logic cannot follow the established SCP-R-001 pattern without discovering the missing helper.
findings.mitigation: Add scp_r_002_results_at(input_value, now_ns) to scp_r_002_test.rego following the SCP-R-001 pattern: 'scp_r_002_results_at(input_value, now_ns) := results if { results := [finding | some finding in main.deny with input as input_value with main.scp_r_002_now_ns as now_ns; finding.rule_id == "SCP-R-002"] }'. Add a boundary test using expires_at set to a specific timestamp and now_ns set to that same timestamp to confirm the <= boundary fires (deny) versus one nanosecond earlier (allow).
